candidate_claim: Legal source experience can preserve local one-step prediction while selectively changing how action-conditioned transition operators compose on unexecuted counterfactual sequences.

evidence.heldout_cascade: Official TD-MPC2 mt30-48M walker-run cascade loses 19.1/19.3 percent versus random and 19.3/18.2 percent versus same-action-multiset shuffled controls, with lower one-step error; cup-catch and walker-run-backwards do not replicate.
evidence.commutator: The native two-step latent commutator does not increase selectively under cascade: walker-run 0.762 cascade versus 0.862 random, cup-catch 0.497 versus 0.505, walker-walk 0.817 versus 0.914.
evidence.worldagen: Released WorldAgen weights show indirect goal-to-input-action-to-world dependence after the direct goal-to-world path is masked, but this is an architecture audit with no attack-specific task loss.

distinguishing_invariant: A composition defect must exceed the Lipschitz-weighted accumulation of local one-step errors on unobserved action permutations while matching observed-support predictions.

novelty_review.reason: The umbrella combines ordinary multi-step exposure/compounding error, policy-conditioned input leakage, and a structural noncommutativity claim that the commutator diagnostic does not support.

scope: Held-out TD-MPC2 task-family boundary and mechanism diagnostic; no scale-up.
